chatgpt.label: Auto — Menu shows Instant 5.3 and Thinking 5.4

final_prompt.title: Copy Final Prompt
final_prompt.description_text: Paste this into your AI product to generate your final question set.
final_prompt.prompt_body:
Display all questions accepted and finalized in this session, in the order they were accepted. Exclude rejected questions and unselected alternatives.

For each question, include:

1. A short, numbered question title
2. The complete question stem
3. All four answer options labeled A–D, with the correct answer first and bolded

Preserve the full text of every accepted question word for word, without shortening, summarizing, or revising anything. Present the questions directly in the chat as ordinary text, without using built-in tools or specialized interfaces.

Do not generate any new questions.

next_question.title: Accept & Continue
next_question.description_text: Accept this question and generate the next one.
next_question.prompt_body: I accept this question. Add it to the working list of accepted questions, preserving its exact wording. Then generate the next question, following any previously established instructions unless I tell you otherwise. Generate only one next question, then pause.

replace_question.title: Generate Alternatives
replace_question.description_text: Generate replacement versions of this question.
replace_question.prompt_body:
Generate five possible replacements for the current question. Make each one meaningfully different while staying within the established scope and instructions.

1. Create one alternative that assesses the same key concept in a different way.
2. Create two alternatives that approach the same subtopic from different nursing practice perspectives (e.g., prioritization/triage; delegation/scope; assessment findings & interpretation; diagnostic findings; interventions/management; evaluating outcomes; questioning/clarifying orders; patient/caregiver teaching; pharmacology & medication safety; ethical/legal; health promotion & risk reduction; safety & infection prevention; psychosocial care & therapeutic communication; communication/documentation & care coordination; developmentally appropriate care; basic care & comfort; procedures/skills & equipment). Choose perspectives that are relevant to the subtopic rather than trying to cover every category.
3. Create two alternatives that explore other important aspects of the same subtopic.

Present all five as complete questions, numbered 1–5 before each question name, so I can easily identify which version I want to keep. Do not add any of them to the accepted question list until I make a selection.

Once I select an alternative by number, treat that alternative as the current draft and display it again in full (question title, complete stem, and all answer options) for my review. Then pause. Only accept this draft and advance when I clearly approve or ask for the next question (e.g., 'next question' or 'continue'). If I request revisions, revise the selected question and show it again for review.

rebalance_content.title: Topic Coverage Audit
rebalance_content.prompt_body:
Pause and audit the topic coverage of my current set of accepted questions. Based on the existing questions and any previously established context, identify the relevant subtopics and present a table showing how many accepted questions address each one.

Then suggest 10 relevant subtopics that currently have no questions, prioritizing concepts important to nursing practice and NCLEX preparation. The goal is to help me rebalance the distribution of questions across subtopics.

Only accept and move to the next question when I clearly approve or ask to continue.

Use only previously accepted questions; exclude the unfinished draft and unselected alternatives. Afterward, if a draft was in progress, redisplay it unchanged in full (title, stem, and all answer options), then pause. Do not accept or advance without my clear approval or request for the next question.

core_or_peripheral.title: Breadth Audit
core_or_peripheral.description_text: Classify questions as core or peripheral in focus.
core_or_peripheral.prompt_body:
Pause and audit my current set of accepted questions for breadth of coverage. Classify the subtopic of each question as one of the following:

Core: Foundational, commonly encountered, or high-priority concepts and clinical decisions within the content area.

Peripheral: Less commonly emphasized but still relevant and clinically important aspects of the content area.

Present the results in a table with the following columns:

1. Question number
2. Focus — Core or Peripheral
3. Subtopic covered — 2–4 word description
4. Suggestion — For each core question, suggest a peripheral angle within the same content area that has not yet been covered.

The goal is to help me evaluate whether my question set covers both essential concepts and less commonly tested but clinically relevant material.

Only accept and move to the next question when I clearly approve or ask to continue.

Use only previously accepted questions; exclude the unfinished draft and unselected alternatives. Afterward, if a draft was in progress, redisplay it unchanged in full (title, stem, and all answer options), then pause. Do not accept or advance without my clear approval or request for the next question.

rebalance_question_type.title: Question Type Audit
rebalance_question_type.description_text: Analyze the distribution of question types.
rebalance_question_type.prompt_body:
Pause and audit my current set of accepted questions for balance across different nursing practice perspectives.

Classify each question according to its primary nursing practice perspective (e.g., prioritization/triage; delegation/scope; assessment findings & interpretation; diagnostic findings; interventions/management; evaluating outcomes; questioning/clarifying orders; patient/caregiver teaching; pharmacology & medication safety; ethical/legal; health promotion & risk reduction; safety & infection prevention; psychosocial care & therapeutic communication; communication/documentation & care coordination; developmentally appropriate care; basic care & comfort; procedures/skills & equipment).

Present the results in a table with the following four columns:

1. Question number — The number of the accepted question.
2. Question focus — A brief, 2–5 word description identifying the question.
3. Nursing practice perspective — The category that best describes the question's current focus.
4. Suggestion for rebalancing — Suggest how the question could be modified to address a different, underrepresented nursing practice perspective while remaining relevant to the same subtopic.

Only suggest changes that would meaningfully improve the balance of nursing practice perspectives across my current set of accepted questions.

Only accept and move to the next question when I clearly approve or ask to continue.

Use only previously accepted questions; exclude the unfinished draft and unselected alternatives. Afterward, if a draft was in progress, redisplay it unchanged in full (title, stem, and all answer options), then pause. Do not accept or advance without my clear approval or request for the next question.

difficulty_audit.title: Difficulty Audit
difficulty_audit.description_text: Analyze the distribution of difficulty levels.
difficulty_audit.prompt_body:
Pause and audit my current set of accepted questions for difficulty. Classify each question as Easy, Moderate, or Hard based on the cognitive demand, complexity of the clinical reasoning required, and plausibility of the distractors.

Present the results in a table with the following columns:

1. Question number — The number of the accepted question.
2. Question focus — A brief, 2–5 word description identifying the question.
3. Difficulty — Easy, Moderate, or Hard.
4. Suggestion — Recommend how the question could be made easier or harder, if doing so would improve the overall balance.

Summarize the number and percentage of questions at each difficulty level.

Only suggest changes that would meaningfully improve the balance of difficulty levels across my current set of accepted questions.

Only accept and move to the next question when I clearly approve or ask to continue.

Use only previously accepted questions; exclude the unfinished draft and unselected alternatives. Afterward, if a draft was in progress, redisplay it unchanged in full (title, stem, and all answer options), then pause. Do not accept or advance without my clear approval or request for the next question.

blooms_taxonomy_audit.title: Bloom’s Level Audit
blooms_taxonomy_audit.description_text: Analyze the distribution of Bloom’s taxonomy levels.
blooms_taxonomy_audit.prompt_body:
Pause and audit my current set of accepted questions for Bloom's taxonomy alignment. Classify each question according to the primary cognitive level required to answer it correctly (Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate, or Create).

Present the results in a table with the following columns:

1. Question number — The number of the accepted question.
2. Question focus — A brief, 2–5 word description identifying the question.
3. Bloom's level — The primary cognitive level required.
4. Suggestion — Recommend how the question could be modified to target a different cognitive level, if doing so would improve the overall balance.

Summarize the number and percentage of questions at each Bloom's level.

Only suggest changes that would meaningfully improve the balance of cognitive levels across my current set of accepted questions.

Only accept and move to the next question when I clearly approve or ask to continue.

Use only previously accepted questions; exclude the unfinished draft and unselected alternatives. Afterward, if a draft was in progress, redisplay it unchanged in full (title, stem, and all answer options), then pause. Do not accept or advance without my clear approval or request for the next question.

correct_answer_options.title: Refine Correct Answer
correct_answer_options.description_text: Generate alternate versions of the correct answer.
correct_answer_options.prompt_body:
Generate 8 versions of the correct answer for the current question.

For option 1, revise the original correct answer to better match the distractors in length, complexity, and style while preserving its original meaning as closely as possible.

For options 2–8, generate seven additional variations of the correct answer, exploring different ways to express the same underlying concept. Each option must remain accurate and unambiguously correct while being similar in length, complexity, and style to the distractors.

Present all 8 options as a numbered list (1–8) so I can easily indicate which version I would like to keep. Do not modify the current question until I make a selection.

Once I select a version, update the current draft and display the complete question (title, stem, and all answer options) for my review. Then pause; only accept and advance when I clearly approve or ask to continue.

distractor_options.title: Refine Distractors
distractor_options.prompt_body:
I want to improve the distractors for the current question. Generate 15 distractor options.

For options 1–3, reproduce the three original distractors, revising them as needed to better match the correct answer in length, complexity, and style. Preserve their original meaning as closely as possible.

For options 4–15, generate 12 additional plausible distractors that are similar in length, complexity, and style to the correct answer. All distractors must be incorrect but plausible alternatives that a nursing student might reasonably consider.

Present all 15 options as a numbered list (1–15) so I can easily indicate which ones I would like to keep.

Once I select the distractors to use, update the current draft and display the complete question (title, stem, and all answer options) for my review. Then pause; only accept and advance when I clearly approve or ask to continue.

pause_review.title: Review Questions
pause_review.description_text: Show all accepted questions so far.
pause_review.prompt_body:
Pause and display all questions I have accepted so far in this session, in the order they were accepted.

For each question, include its numbered title, complete question stem, and all four answer options labeled A–D, with the correct answer first and bolded.

Preserve the full text of every accepted question word for word, without shortening, summarizing, or revising anything. Do not include rejected questions or unselected alternatives.

Only accept and move to the next question when I clearly approve or ask to continue.

Use only previously accepted questions; exclude the unfinished draft and unselected alternatives. Afterward, if a draft was in progress, redisplay it unchanged in full (title, stem, and all answer options), then pause. Do not accept or advance without my clear approval or request for the next question.

sample_copy_style.title: Match Question Style
sample_copy_style.description_text: Use sample questions as exemplars for the AI to follow.
sample_copy_style.prompt_body:
I’m going to provide some sample questions. Study them carefully and use them as a reference for the style, structure, and difficulty of the questions you generate, without copying their content too closely. Continue following any previously established instructions unless I tell you otherwise.

Only accept and move to the next question when I clearly approve or ask to continue.

I will paste the sample questions below.

sample_new_version.title: Create New Versions
sample_new_version.description_text: Use sample questions to create different versions on the same topics.
sample_new_version.prompt_body:
I’m going to provide some sample questions. Create new versions of these questions that assess the same underlying concepts. Change the wording, scenarios, and answer options so the new questions are meaningfully different from the originals. Continue following any previously established instructions unless I tell you otherwise.

Only accept and move to the next question when I clearly approve or ask to continue.

I will paste the sample questions below.

sample_supplement.title: Supplement Question Set
sample_supplement.description_text: Use sample questions to create new questions on the same content area without overlap.
sample_supplement.prompt_body:
I’m going to provide some sample questions. Use them to set the goals for the scope, style, and priorities of the new questions. Generate additional questions that complement the samples by addressing relevant concepts, subtopics, or clinical applications not already covered. Avoid simply rewording existing questions or repeating the same scenarios or answer logic. The new questions should broaden coverage while fitting naturally alongside the originals. Continue following any previously established instructions unless I tell you otherwise.

Only accept and move to the next question when I clearly approve or ask to continue.

I will paste the sample questions below.

sample_practice.title: Prepare Practice Questions
sample_practice.description_text: Use sample exam questions to create practice questions.
sample_practice.prompt_body:
I’m going to provide some sample questions from an exam that students will take. Use them to identify the exam's content areas, priorities, and key concepts, then create a set of practice questions that will help students prepare for the exam.

Some overlap in content is appropriate, but avoid closely rewriting the exam questions or creating questions so narrowly matched that they teach to the test. Instead, focus on developing students' understanding of the underlying concepts and their ability to apply them in different situations.

Include a mix of foundational questions that build understanding and more challenging questions that require application and critical thinking. Broaden coverage by including relevant subtopics not directly represented in the samples and by approaching familiar concepts from different angles, such as interventions instead of assessment or patient teaching instead of pharmacology.

Continue following any previously established instructions unless I tell you otherwise.

Only accept and move to the next question when I clearly approve or ask to continue.

I will paste the sample questions below.

starter.title: Copy starter prompt
starter.description_text: Paste this into your selected LLM to begin generating questions.
starter.prompt_body:
I am a nursing school instructor and would like your help creating multiple-choice questions for my class. Use the following parameters:
1. Class Context: {{COURSE}}
2. Content Area: {{AREA}}
3. Desired Number of Questions: {{QUESTION_COUNT}}
4. Additional parameters to consider (if blank, ignore): {{NOTES_LINE}}

I may also provide documents to guide question creation. Use them as a general reference, but do not rely on them exclusively. Create a question set that emphasizes concepts within the content area that are most relevant to NCLEX and nursing practice, while following best practices for high-quality multiple-choice item writing.

When presenting questions, display them directly in the chat as ordinary text. Do not use built-in tools such as interactive quizzes or other specialized interfaces. Do not shorten, summarize, or truncate questions. Always preserve the full text of each question, word for word, unless I explicitly request revisions.

Present each question in the following order (do not include these labels in your output):
Question Name
Question Stem
A. The correct answer.
B. The first distractor.
C. The second distractor.
D. The third distractor.

You will create one question at a time. Pause after each one so I can give feedback on the overall question set or on the individual question just generated. Revise when asked. Only accept and move on when I clearly approve or ask for the next question (e.g., 'next question' or 'continue'); choosing an option or requesting edits alone is not approval.

For now, respond with a table that outlines the plan for all of the questions with these headings: #; subtopic; key concept. I will let you know if I would like any adjustments before you begin writing questions.
